sections.overview: The Seraphim is a geometrid moth found across parts of Europe.
sections.identification: The male has conspicuous lobes on the hindwings. It can be confused with the paler, more uniform Early Tooth-striped (*Trichopteryx carpinata*), which lacks its broad dark basal forewing band.
sections.habitat: In Britain, adults inhabit woodland and fly mainly in spring; larvae feed on aspen and other poplars.
sections.diet: The caterpillars feed on aspen (*Populus tremula*) and other poplars (*Populus* spp.).
sections.behavior: Adults are attracted to light, which helps explain records from moth-trapping surveys.
sections.reproduction: The reviewed accounts describe the adult flight and larval food plants but give no egg-laying details.
sections.ecology: Local occurrence can track the distribution of its food trees, as regional records note for aspen and poplars.
sections.conservation: A French regional database lists no threat evaluation and warns that its regional presence data have not been consolidated by experts; this is not a global assessment.
